item.title: International Business in a Reconfiguring Southeast Asia
item.content:encoded:
S. Tamer Cavusgil, Georgia State University

Southeast Asia is a critical yet underrepresented region in international business research, despite hosting the world's fifth-largest economic bloc and attracting record foreign investment. The region's distinctive characteristics—diverse political systems, family capitalism networks, state-linked enterprises, and rapid digital development—challenge existing international business theory but remain largely absent from leading journals.

This focused issue invites contributions that treat Southeast Asian phenomena as theoretically generative rather than merely illustrative, particularly welcoming scholars based in the region. The collection addresses four themes: internationalization of Southeast Asian multinationals, supply chain reconfiguration, geopolitical hedging strategies amid great-power competition, and indigenous theorizing drawing on Southeast Asian intellectual traditions to advance broader international business literature.

Appel publié par Management International Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Internationalization of Southeast Asian multinationals
  • Springboard and asset-augmentation strategies of ASEAN MNEs
  • Digital-native champions and platform architecture
  • State-linked enterprises internationalization
  • Supply chain reconfiguration and global value chain integration
  • Maritime connectivity and port competitiveness
  • Supply chain resilience and logistics
  • Cross-border trade and geopolitical hedging
  • Non-market strategy under strategic ambiguity
  • Middle-power firms and neutral coordination hubs
  • Indigenous theorizing and Southeast Asian intellectual traditions
  • Multi-language qualitative research methods
  • Postcolonial perspectives on knowledge production
  • Ethnographic and historical-archival fieldwork
